module_title: School Management Committees (SMC) & SDP: Legal Foundations
introduction: This foundational level introduces the School Management Committee (SMC) and the School Development Plan (SDP) as the primary tools for community participation and decentralized governance in Indian schools, legally mandated by the RTE Act 2009.

core_concepts.title: What is a School Management Committee (SMC)?
core_concepts.description:
Mandated by **Section 21** of the Right to Education (RTE) Act 2009, an SMC is a statutory body established in every government, government-aided, and special category school. 
- Core Purpose: To decentralize school governance by shifting power away from distant bureaucrats and giving it to the local community, specifically the parents, to monitor school operations.

core_concepts.title: Composition of the SMC (The 75% and 50% Rules)
core_concepts.description:
This is the most highly tested area in CTET and KVS exams. The RTE Act prescribes a strict demographic composition to ensure grassroots representation:
1. 75% Parents: At least three-fourths (75%) of the SMC members MUST be parents or guardians of the children studying in that school.
2. 50% Women: Out of the total members, at least 50% MUST be women.
3. Disadvantaged Representation: There must be proportionate representation from parents of children belonging to disadvantaged groups and weaker sections.

core_concepts.title: What is the School Development Plan (SDP)?
core_concepts.description:
Mandated by **Section 22** of the RTE Act. The SDP is the primary official document prepared by the SMC.
- It is a comprehensive plan detailing the school's requirements for infrastructure, financial grants, and teacher deployment.
- Importance: The SDP acts as the absolute basis upon which the State Government or Local Authority releases grants and funds to the school.

core_concepts.title: Core Functions of the SMC
core_concepts.description:
Under the RTE Act, the SMC has three primary duties:
1. Monitor the working of the school (attendance, mid-day meals, infrastructure).
2. Prepare and recommend the School Development Plan (SDP).
3. Monitor the utilization of financial grants received from the government or other sources.

important_entities.name: Unaided Private Schools Exemption
important_entities.key_fact: Unaided private schools do not fall under Section 21.
important_entities.significance: Under the RTE Act, unaided private schools are NOT legally required to form an SMC in the exact demographic format prescribed for government schools. They have their own managing committees, though state rules may vary.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will ask: 'Which of the following is NOT a function of the SMC?' Options will include 'Monitoring grants', 'Preparing SDP', and 'Designing the daily academic timetable / Evaluating the teacher's pedagogical skills'. The correct answer is the latter. The SMC manages operations, funds, and basic rights; it does NOT interfere in the professional academic and pedagogical micro-management of the classroom.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 21 creates the Committee, 22 creates the Plan
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the sequential legal order: First, you must form the SMC (Section 21), and then the SMC sits down to make the SDP (Section 22).

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever an exam asks for the required percentage of parents/guardians in an SMC under the RTE Act, unconditionally select **75%**.
